title: Google Play adds private, AI-built Android apps
friendlyTitle: Google Play will run personal apps without making them public
summary: Google Play is adding personal apps that a user can build with tools such as Google AI Studio and run on their own Android device without publishing them publicly. The initial rollout is for US users aged 18 and over, with trusted sharing planned later.
friendlySummary: Adults in the US can start putting AI-built apps on their own Android phones without listing them for everyone. Google plans to add sharing with trusted people later.
whyItMatters: This removes a distribution hurdle for small apps built around one person’s routine, hobby or work process. Private distribution reduces exposure, but the app still needs careful permission, data and security review because generated code runs on a personal device.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This makes small personal apps easier to use. You should still check what data and phone permissions each app can access.
